what_this_is: Per tool, the top-level keys a LIVE response carries that the tool's contract card does not name, each with the reason it is missing from aihub#412's corpus. A card's response_keys_observed is copied from a GENERATED corpus record (docs/audits/aihub-412-corpus-facts/response-keys/), so a key the server started emitting after the corpus was extracted cannot be added to the card without hand-editing a generated file. It is declared here instead. K10 in internal/mcp/card_response_keys_live_e2e_db_test.go checks this file by EQUALITY against (live keys minus card keys): an undeclared live key fails, an invented entry fails, an entry the card has since absorbed fails as redundant, and an entry for a key the server no longer emits fails as stale. Every entry is documentation debt against the card, and maxUndeclaredLiveKeys in that file is the ceiling on it.
how_to_regenerate: AIHUB_TEST_DB=... PF_LIVE_KEYS_REGEN=1 go test ./internal/mcp/ -run TestE2ELiveResponseKeys — then replace the placeholder reason on every new entry by hand; the gate rejects the placeholder.

pf_adopt_artifact.event_id: The tool was published and never called in the corpus window, so it has no corpus record at all and its card carries response_keys_observed=null (K7 CORPUS_INVENTED refuses a card that lists keys the corpus has no record of). The handler returns the jsonResult of the event it emits, which is this one key.

pf_claim_work_item.id: Restored by aihub#388 (PR #344, landed 2026-09-07), which rewrote the claim projection from a keep-list to a delete-list; the corpus's 788 claims were answered by the keep-list, which dropped this field in silence.
pf_claim_work_item.requires_human_session: Same aihub#388 rewrite. This is the field the post-claim routing rule branches on, and the keep-list dropped it, so the corpus never saw it.
pf_claim_work_item.step_recovery_hint: Same aihub#388 rewrite; omitempty, non-empty whenever there is a hint.

pf_close_artifact.event_id: Published and never called in the corpus window, so no corpus record and a null card list. The handler returns the emitted event's jsonResult.

pf_create_project.members_version: domain.Project gained this field with aihub#260's compare-and-set guard (PR #289, landed 2026-09-02). The corpus holds exactly one pf_create_project call, made 2026-08-15, before the field existed.

pf_force_takeover.id: Restored by aihub#422 (PR #365, landed 2026-09-08), which replaced the five-key keep-list with a delete-list; the corpus's 18 takeovers all predate it, the last on 2026-09-06.

pf_ignore_artifact.event_id: Published and never called in the corpus window, so no corpus record and a null card list. The handler returns the emitted event's jsonResult.

pf_resolve_commit.ok: Published and never called in the corpus window (annotations are answered through the /ui viewer), so no corpus record and a null card list.

pf_rotate_identifier.plain: Published and never called in the corpus window, so no corpus record and a null card list.
pf_rotate_identifier.prefix: Published and never called in the corpus window, so no corpus record and a null card list.

pf_update_project.members_version: Same aihub#260 field as pf_create_project above (PR #289, landed 2026-09-02). The corpus's 22 pf_update_project calls end on 2026-09-01, the day before.

pf_update_user.ok: Published and never called in the corpus window, so no corpus record and a null card list.
